# Phase Two — Gevurah Critique

The Awtsmoos gives light without surrendering boundary; Awtsmoos.com must keep glass alive without draining battery, obscuring text, or reintroducing visual clutter.

## Twenty constraints and improvements
1. Do not animate blur values.
2. Do not animate large background-position fields continuously.
3. Do not stack more than one ambient pseudo-layer on a surface.
4. Check existing pseudo-element ownership before choosing before/after.
5. Prefer dedicated wrapper-free selectors only where pseudo-elements are unused.
6. Keep specular opacity below text-interference levels.
7. Keep pointer-events disabled on decorative layers.
8. Keep overflow clipping local to rounded glass surfaces.
9. Preserve focus rings above decorative light.
10. Preserve readable contrast on dark mobile backgrounds.
11. Keep ambient animation periods long enough to feel calm.
12. Let interaction glints complete in under half a second.
13. Let disclosure reveal motion complete in under a quarter second.
14. Keep route navigation response tactile but not bouncy.
15. Do not add JavaScript for effects CSS can express safely.
16. Keep each new CSS module under 120 lines.
17. Use tabs throughout touched CSS.
18. Give each touched file B"H, Awtsmoos, and Awtsmoos.com documentation.
19. Bump the entire stylesheet cache generation together.
20. Run existing reduced-motion/browser contracts after implementation.

## Architecture
- `glass-motion.css`: import-only covenant.
- `glass-motion-surfaces.css`: static glass and ambient sheen.
- `glass-motion-interactions.css`: Create, route, disclosure-summary tactile motion.
- `glass-motion-reveal.css`: opened-detail/content manifestation.
- `glass-motion-accessibility.css`: reduced motion/transparency/forced colors.

The boundary is not the enemy of beauty. Gevurah gives the shimmer a vessel so Tiferes can make it useful.
